title: Intermittent tenant fanout 5xx — rapid trace capture, safe rollback hotpatch, and customer communication
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
High-severity customer escalations reported intermittent 502/504 and long tail timeouts for a subset of tenants during heavy concurrent request bursts. Users saw repeated failures as client SDK retries amplified the load. This ticket coordinates rapid triage, a safe hotpatch rollout, and longer-term mitigations across edge, runtime, and SDK settings.

Investigation notes:
- Timeline: multiple escalations between 2026-03-08 21:00 UTC and 2026-03-09 03:00 UTC from three large tenants.
- Symptom set: spikes in upstream connection errors from edge proxies to runtime (502/504), sudden increases in per-tenant inflight connections, KV cache compaction events correlated with error windows, and visible retry storms from SDKs.
- Root cause hypothesis: when a tenant produced high parallel streaming/fanout requests (large batch uploads + live chat fanout), edge admission control failed to cap per-tenant concurrency. Upstream connection churn + short-lived connections hit ephemeral port pressure and backend proxies returned 502/504. Client SDKs retried with default aggressive backoff, amplifying the surge and causing partial regional saturation.

Immediate mitigations applied (hotpatch):
1) Edge hotpatch (deployed 2026-03-10 04:00 UTC) to cap per-tenant concurrent upstream connections and queue excess for short window (configurable soft limit).
2) Introduced short-lived in-edge request fingerprint to dedupe immediate retry amplification (best-effort de-dup on same idempotency token).
3) Emergency SDK guidance pushed to customers: set retry backoff to linear for 30s and enable idempotency tokens for operations until final fix.
These mitigations reduced visible 5xx rates by ~78% in the following 12 hours per monitoring.

Planned long-term fixes:
- Add robust per-tenant admission controller at the edge with hysteresis (priority-based queuing and fair-share).
- Improve keepalive and upstream connection pooling to reduce ephemeral port churn.
- Add server-side retry hysteresis: detect tenant-origin retry storms and reduce retry acceptance or fast-fail with clear 429 guidance.
- Strengthen KV cache compaction telemetry to avoid compaction overlap with high-fanout windows.

Acceptance criteria:
- No recurring tenant-visible 502/504 bursts for same tenants under same workload pattern for 72 hours post-rollout.
- Per-tenant inflight connection graphs show soft-limit enforcement and reduced tail latencies.
- Post-deploy dashboards include per-tenant retry amplification metric and automated alert if >2x baseline.
- SDK guidance and release notes issued to customers and support team.

Artifacts and links:
- Incident dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/hosted-incidents/tenant-fanout-2026-03
- Hotpatch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge/pull/4827
- Edge admission design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Edge+per-tenant+admission+controller
- Postmortem draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/PM-295412+postmortem

Rollback plan:
- Hotpatch is staged: can be rolled back by reverting PR 4827 with automated traffic drain (5 minutes) and traffic fail-open to prior admission behavior. Run rollback if error rate or latency regressions exceed thresholds (error_rate > baseline + 10% for 30m).

Next steps / owner assignments:
- Luca: complete edge admission controller follow-up RFC and land initial rate-limiter (estimate 8 pts).
- Mei (SRE): add per-tenant retry-amplification alert and refine dashboards.
- Priya (PM): coordinate customer comms and update escalation template.
- Dev team: produce end-to-end chaos test to reproduce fanout failure pattern in staging.
